anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level statements or transaction design force the engine to touch far more data, rows, or time than the business requirement demands.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer metadata no longer reflects real data distribution, causing systematic cardinality and cost misestimation that leads to poor plan choices.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes consume an abnormally large share of CPU, saturating host compute capacity and slowing all work.

When these three root causes appear together, symptoms overlap and intensify: the same SQLs dominate slow-query and CPU-time lists, their execution plans show severe row-estimate errors, and each run consumes many more CPU cycles than expected. Global host metrics hover near 100 % utilization with long run queues, while engine views report both scheduler waits and wide discrepancies between estimated and actual row counts. Automatic statistics jobs and background maintenance fall behind because of CPU starvation, causing fresh data changes to remain un-analyzed. End-user sessions experience extreme and erratic latency, timeouts, and transaction rollbacks, and any plan change—good or bad—can swing performance unpredictably.

Causally, inefficient workload logic initiates excessive data access. Stale or incomplete statistics then misinform the optimizer, amplifying the inefficiency by selecting full scans, Cartesian joins, or over-parallelized plans. The compounded CPU demand drives the server into sustained saturation, which in turn delays automatic statistics refresh tasks and forces the optimizer to rely even longer on bad metadata, closing a feedback loop that continually degrades plan quality. High CPU pressure also slows individual query execution, keeping transactions open longer and further increasing contention and resource demand. The interaction of bad logic, bad statistics, and exhausted CPU thus produces a self-reinforcing spiral that can cripple both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds the server waits for activity on an interactive connection before closing it.
entry.trigger_condition: An interactive session remains idle longer than interactive_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The server closes the idle interactive connection.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
